milestoneTitle: Segment/solution pages and enquiry flows (owners, installers, professionals)
description: Documented scope proposal for MC-19/36. The roadmap row and the MC-18→MC-19 handoff define the objective and the audience segments, but they do not define an authoritative MC-19 Master Prompt, the exact page/route/entity set, the content contract, the CTA behaviour or the enquiry-flow design. The owners segment has no MC-15 proposed route, and every enquiry/lead flow is blocked by the open privacy gate. Implementation is therefore not started; this package is the required prerequisite input for a later authorized execution.
generationMethod: Authored from the verified repository state at MC-18 HEAD 3490c0f71eb6eaa89588b7a6d75bb3b6066cd094, the 36-milestone registry, the MC-18 delivery/audit package, the MC-18→MC-19 handoff inputs, the MC-15 proposed route registry and the MC-14 release-evidence gates. No implementation file was created or modified.
knownLimitations: This is a proposal, not an MC-19 plan, estimate, schedule or approval.
MC-19 implementation has not started: no segment page, solution page, enquiry form, lead endpoint, installer registration or contact channel exists.
The proposal does not create, register or activate any public route, canonical, hreflang, structured data or sitemap entry.
The recommended option is conditional on an explicitly issued MC-19 Master Prompt and a recorded IA/route decision; it is not self-approving.

External approvals (trademark, public use, source IP, public copy, claims, privacy, commercial data, publication, MC-14 gate programme) remain absent and are not reinterpreted as internal implementation approval.

definitionAssessment.reason: The authoritative MC-19 Master Prompt is not recorded in the repository or supplied in this milestone mandate; the 36-prompt registry explicitly marks prompts 03-36 as planning placeholders, but a repository search alone cannot prove non-issuance because MC-18 records the same uncommitted-prompt gap. The stop decision also rests on independently verifiable blockers: the roadmap row and handoff define the objective and audiences but not the exact page set, route/entity identities, content contract, CTA behaviour or enquiry-flow design; the owners segment has no MC-15 route/entity/page type; and enquiry/lead flows are blocked by the open privacy gate.
defined: High-level objective: segment/solution pages and enquiry flows for owners, installers and professionals (registry row 19; handoff section 6).
Expected output: segment pages + lead flows (registry row 19).
Verification theme: real CTAs only, per readiness (registry row 19).
Three audience references reserved by MC-18: OWNERS, INSTALLERS, PROFESSIONAL_FLEETS (handoff section 6).
Reuse constraint: MC-17 design system and the single bilingual component tree, no fork (handoff section 17).
Publication constraint: no public route, canonical, hreflang, JSON-LD or sitemap entry before the gates and release authorization (handoff sections 11 and 17).
Privacy constraint: no enquiry/lead flow before privacy approval, DPA, DPIA, consent, minimisation, anti-abuse and security review (handoff section 9).
Non-goals: no price, stock, purchase, certification, testimonial, sea-trial or licensing claim; no merge, deploy or publication (handoff section 17).
undefined: Authoritative MC-19 Master Prompt text and its exact deliverables. The registry states that prompts 03-36 are planning placeholders and the client-issued Master Prompt is authoritative; the prompt is not recorded here, and repository absence cannot prove it was never issued uncommitted.
Exact page set: three segment pages, two MC-15 professional pages, the MC-15 solutions overview and/or the six bundle solution pages are all plausible readings of 'segment/solution pages'.
Route/entity/page-type identities for an owners page and a professional-fleets page; MC-15 defines 'professionals' and 'installers' but no 'owners' route.
Bilingual content contract, copy ownership, evidence registry and section structure for each page.
CTA behaviour: 'real CTAs only' is stated, but quote/pre-registration require lead capture and a privacy basis that does not exist; 'coming-soon' has no defined design or acceptance test.
Enquiry/lead-flow design, lawful basis, consent capture, retention, anti-abuse, endpoint security and data minimisation.
Measured acceptance thresholds and the exact test matrix for MC-19.
Whether MC-19 solution pages duplicate or overlap MC-23 bundle comparison and MC-20-22 family pages.
Publication and indexation authorization for any MC-19 route.

options.title: Internal audience pages without enquiry flows (recommended)
pages: OWNERS segment page (ES/EN, one component tree)
INSTALLERS segment page (ES/EN, MC-15 'installers' identity unless the IA decision changes it)
PROFESSIONAL_FLEETS segment page (ES/EN, FLEET remains a contracted solution)
options.solutionContext: Embedded per-segment bundle/family context reusing the MC-18 presentation; no separate bundle detail routes in MC-19.
options.ctas: Informational navigation and fail-closed 'coming soon / not for sale' presentation only; no quote, pre-registration, form or lead capture.
options.newRoutes: Provisional: owners and professional-fleets identities require an IA decision; installers can reuse the MC-15 proposed route. No public registration in this milestone.
options.rationale: Smallest complete internal scope that matches the three declared audiences, preserves every gate and avoids blocking on privacy. Enquiry flows are explicitly deferred.

options.title: MC-15-aligned professional and solution pages
options.ctas: Informational and fail-closed; no enquiry flow.
options.newRoutes: Reuses MC-15 proposed identities but still requires a scope decision against MC-20-23 (family pages and bundle comparison) to avoid duplicate page ownership.
options.rationale: Closer to the literal 'solution pages' wording, but it overlaps MC-20-23 and is not the smallest scope. It also does not resolve the missing owners route.

options.title: Full MC-07B scope including enquiry and lead flows
options.ctas: Real quote/pre-registration CTAs with server-authoritative, privacy-approved handling.
options.newRoutes: Not determinable before the IA decision.
options.rationale: Not executable now: lead capture is prohibited until privacy/DPA/DPIA approval exists, and publication is not authorized.

recommendation: Do not implement MC-19 until P01 (authoritative Master Prompt), P02 (IA decision for the segment/solution route set) and P10 (explicit scope approval) exist. Then execute Option A as an isolated internal preview, reusing the MC-17 design system and MC-18 patterns, with every CTA fail-closed and enquiry/lead flows deferred until P03 and the publication gates close. This is a proposal, not an approval.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.criterion: The accountable owner has issued the MC-19 Master Prompt and approved this scope (P01, P10).
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.verification: Recorded approval with the exact scope revision and owner names.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.criterion: The IA/route decision records every MC-19 route, entity, page type and locale path, including the owners and professional-fleets segments, with a collision check against the 21 existing public route ids and the 23 MC-15 proposed routes (P02).
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.verification: Route decision record plus collision dataset; no public registration.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.criterion: Each approved page exists once as a locale-aware component tree with one bilingual content source; every rendered block has contentId, sectionId, copyClass, evidenceIds, publicationStatus=INTERNAL_DRAFT_NOT_APPROVED and approvalStatus=NOT_APPROVED.
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.verification: TypeScript build plus content validator and ES/EN parity check.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.criterion: MC-17 design-system components are reused without fork or duplicate implementation.
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.verification: Import graph and selector-collision check; design-system diff empty.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.criterion: No public route, sitemap entry, canonical, hreflang, Open Graph, Twitter card or JSON-LD is emitted; the pages are served only by the loopback preview with noindex and a Host allowlist; the production server returns 404 for every MC-19 path.
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.verification: SSR header probes, production build scan and production 404 probes.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.criterion: No enquiry form, input, contact endpoint, lead storage, installer registration, quote request or pre-registration exists while P03 is blocked; CTAs are informational and fail-closed, with no price, stock, purchase, certification or availability claim.
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.verification: Form/input/endpoint scan, claim guard scan and adversarial mutations.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.criterion: SSR and hydration agree in both locales; keyboard navigation, visible focus, reduced motion and responsive layout 320-1440 pass the agreed automated checks, with manual accessibility limits disclosed.
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.verification: Playwright SSR/hydration, responsive and keyboard runs; axe results with stated limits.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.criterion: All relevant gates run with exact counts: typecheck, deterministic validator, unit/adversarial suite, Playwright, public build, i18n/commerce/SEO/backup regressions and production isolation.
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.verification: Recorded commands, exit codes and counts; no prefixed PASS.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.criterion: An independent reviewer who did not implement the pages reviews the real diff and evidence; 0 BLOCKING and 0 MAJOR findings remain open.
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.verification: Independent review record plus review-findings dataset.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.criterion: Delivery stays in a draft PR stacked on the verified MC-18 branch; no merge, deployment, publication, sitemap submission or public MAREA activation; every governance flag and inherited debt item remains visible.
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.verification: PR state, git history, public build scan, governance flag check and inherited-debt register.
